PullRequest.Title: Offer Compare when saving a notebook that changed on disk
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Refs #344849

## Problem

When a notebook has unsaved changes and its file changes on disk (an agent, git, a script), saving shows "Failed to save 'analysis.ipynb': The content of the file is newer. Do you want to overwrite the file with your changes?" with only **Overwrite** and **Revert**. A dirty notebook never shows the change on disk, so the user cannot see what **Overwrite** throws away, and Overwrite looks like the right choice. Text files in the same situation get a **Compare** action that opens a diff of the file on disk against the editor.

## Root cause

Notebooks are backed by stored file working copies, and the stored file working copy builds its own save error notification. For a save conflict (`FILE_MODIFIED_SINCE`) it only adds Overwrite and Revert:
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c8a3f819b4a13366d5846a02288ab53b4d89ac50/src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/common/storedFileWorkingCopy.ts#L1150-L1156

Text files go through `TextFileSaveErrorHandler`, which adds Compare and opens the disk side through a text content provider for the `conflictResolution` scheme:
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c8a3f819b4a13366d5846a02288ab53b4d89ac50/src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/editors/textFileSaveErrorHandler.ts#L129-L131
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c8a3f819b4a13366d5846a02288ab53b4d89ac50/src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/editors/textFileSaveErrorHandler.ts#L238-L270

That provider only produces text models, so it can't feed the notebook diff editor, which resolves both sides as notebooks through the file service.

## Fix

- The stored file working copy save conflict notification now offers **Compare**, **Overwrite**, and **Revert**. Compare opens a diff with the file as it is on disk on the left and the working copy on the right, titled "analysis.ipynb (in file) ↔ analysis.ipynb - Resolve save conflict". It uses the editor that shows the working copy (for notebooks, the notebook diff editor of the same notebook type), so the right side is the unsaved notebook.
- Compare is only offered when that editor can open a diff editor. When it can't, the editor resolver falls back to a text diff whose right side is the file on disk rather than the unsaved notebook, so both sides would match and hide what Overwrite keeps. In that case the notification offers only Overwrite and Revert, as before.
- The disk side comes from a new readonly file system provider (`vscode-file-on-disk` scheme, `FileOnDiskFileSystemProvider`) that reads the resource through the file service. This follows the guidance on #194917 that comparisons for custom editors need a file system provider rather than a text content provider. The files contribution registers it, and Compare is only offered when it is registered.
- The disk side follows the file on disk. While the comparison is visible, the provider forwards changes of the file under its own URI through a correlated watcher, so the disk side reloads. Compare also reloads a comparison that is already open before showing it, because the file may have changed while that comparison was in the background.
- The notebook diff editor doesn't recompute while it's the active editor, so typing in it doesn't rebuild the view. That rule now only applies to the modified side. The original side can't be edited in the diff editor, so its changes always come from outside and are shown right away.
- Text files have toolbar actions in their conflict diff to accept or revert. The notebook diff has none, so after Compare opens the diff, the conflict notification is shown again and Overwrite and Revert stay one click away. Overwrite, Revert, the message, and the text file flow are unchanged.

#282368 (draft) proposes a similar readonly provider to fix **Compare with Saved** for notebooks and custom editors. This PR doesn't depend on it and doesn't change Compare with Saved. If both move forward, they can share one provider.

### Other gaps found, not changed here

- A dirty notebook never shows that its file changed on disk. Dirty working copies are not reloaded, so the editor keeps the old cells with no indication until the save fails:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c8a3f819b4a13366d5846a02288ab53b4d89ac50/src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/common/storedFileWorkingCopyManager.ts#L277-L279
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c8a3f819b4a13366d5846a02288ab53b4d89ac50/src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/common/storedFileWorkingCopy.ts#L461-L465
- An external edit that keeps the file the same size is not detected at all, so saving silently overwrites it. The dirty-write check compares an etag built from the old mtime and the new size, so it only reports a conflict when the size changed. This affects text files too:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c8a3f819b4a13366d5846a02288ab53b4d89ac50/src/vs/platform/files/common/fileService.ts#L519-L523
- With screen reader optimization on, or with `notebook.diff.enablePreview` off, notebooks are meant to use a text diff instead of the notebook diff. In practice the notebook diff stays available: the notebook registration always provides it at startup, and the editor resolver keeps a copy of each editor's factories until it re-reads its registrations (for example when another editor registers). After that re-read, this PR doesn't offer Compare, so screen reader users only get Overwrite and Revert, as before. A text comparison backed by the unsaved notebook JSON would let them compare too.

## Before / after

### Before

The notebook has an unsaved edit and a cell was added to the file on disk. Saving shows the conflict with only Overwrite and Revert.

![Before: the notebook save conflict notification offers only Overwrite and Revert](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/08edae3de478469046d3f559fa258ebfdf9994d8/20261015-171820-C22-F1/before.gif?raw=true)

### After

Same steps. The notification offers Compare, and Compare opens the notebook diff: the cell added on disk on the left (red, what Overwrite would discard) and the unsaved edit on the right. Another cell is then added to the file on disk while the diff is open, and it appears in the diff right away. Overwrite then saves the notebook, and the diff shows the file on disk matching the editor.

![After: Compare opens the notebook diff, a second change on disk shows up in it, and Overwrite saves the notebook](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/1f090ed736ae3bdb96bb0b0c0dd81ad90465c886/20261015-171820-C22-F1-r2/after.gif?raw=true)

## How to test

1. Open a `.ipynb` in a dev build and type into a cell so the notebook is dirty. Don't save.
2. From outside VS Code, add a cell to the file on disk (for example with a small script that appends to `cells` and rewrites the JSON).
3. Save the notebook. The error notification offers **Compare**, **Overwrite**, and **Revert**.
4. Select **Compare**. The notebook diff opens with the added cell on the left and your edit on the right. The notification is shown again.
5. With the diff open, add another cell to the file on disk. It appears on the left side of the diff right away.
6. Switch to the notebook tab, change the file on disk again, then select **Compare** in the notification. The diff shows the latest file on disk.
7. **Overwrite** or **Revert** resolves the conflict.
8. To check the case where notebooks can't open a diff: set `notebook.diff.enablePreview` to `false` (or toggle screen reader optimization), then make the editor resolver re-read its registrations, for example by changing `workbench.settings.useSplitJSON`. A new save conflict then offers only **Overwrite** and **Revert**.

<details><summary>Automated repro scenario</summary>

Save as `repro.cjs`, then run `node test/scenario/out/runScenario.js --dev repro.cjs` from the repo root
(fails on main, passes with this PR). The scenario runner disables notification toasts, so the scenario reads the notification in the Notifications Center.

```js
// Save conflict on a notebook: the notification should offer Compare, and Compare
// should open the notebook diff of the file on disk against the unsaved notebook.
const os = require('os');
const path = require('path');
const fs = require('fs');

const workspacePath = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'nb-save-conflict-'));
const notebookPath = path.join(workspacePath, 'analysis.ipynb');

const ADDED_ON_DISK = 'added_on_disk = True';
const CHANGED_AGAIN = 'changed_again = 2';
const TYPED_IN_EDITOR = 'typed_in_editor = 1';

function cell(id, cellType, source) {
	return cellType === 'code'
		? { cell_type: 'code', execution_count: null, id, metadata: {}, outputs: [], source: [source] }
		: { cell_type: 'markdown', id, metadata: {}, source: [source] };
}

const notebook = {
	cells: [
		cell('c1', 'markdown', '# Sales analysis'),
		cell('c2', 'code', 'total = 40 + 2')
	],
	metadata: { language_info: { name: 'python' } },
	nbformat: 4,
	nbformat_minor: 5
};
fs.writeFileSync(notebookPath, JSON.stringify(notebook, null, 1) + '\n');

const CELL_ROWS = '.notebook-editor .cell-list-container .monaco-list-row';
// The scenario runner disables notification toasts, so read notifications in the Notifications Center.
const NOTIFICATION = '.notifications-center .notification-list-item';

async function conflictToast(context) {
	const { page, workbench } = context;
	if (!(await page.locator('.notifications-center').isVisible())) {
		await workbench.quickaccess.runCommand('notifications.showList');
	}
	const toast = page.locator(NOTIFICATION, { hasText: 'The content of the file is newer' }).first();
	await toast.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20000 });
	return toast;
}

async function toastButtons(toast) {
	return (await toast.locator('.monaco-button').allInnerTexts()).map(label => label.trim()).filter(Boolean);
}

module.exports = {
	id: 'notebook-save-conflict-compare',
	title: 'Notebook save conflict offers Compare with the file on disk',
	source: 'https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/344849',
	workspacePath,
	stepPauseMs: 1500,
	userSettings: {
		'files.autoSave': 'off',
		'workbench.startupEditor': 'none',
		'workbench.editor.enablePreview': false,
		'notebook.experimental.enableNewDiffEditor': false,
		'workbench.secondarySideBar.defaultVisibility': 'hidden',
		'chat.disableAIFeatures': true
	},
	steps: [
		{
			id: 'S1',
			title: 'Open a notebook with two cells',
			async run(context) {
				const { page, workbench } = context;
				await workbench.quickaccess.openFileQuickAccessAndWait(notebookPath, 'analysis.ipynb');
				await workbench.quickinput.selectQuickInputElement(0);
				await page.waitForFunction(selector => document.querySelectorAll(selector).length === 2, CELL_ROWS, { timeout: 60000 });
				await page.locator(CELL_ROWS).nth(1).locator('.view-lines').waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20000 });
				return 'The notebook editor shows the two cells from disk.';
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'S2',
			title: 'Edit a cell so the notebook has unsaved changes',
			async run(context) {
				const { page } = context;
				const codeCell = page.locator(CELL_ROWS).nth(1);
				await codeCell.locator('.view-lines').click();
				await page.keyboard.press('End');
				await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
				await page.keyboard.type(TYPED_IN_EDITOR);
				await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
				await page.waitForSelector('.tabs-container .tab.active.dirty', { timeout: 10000 });
				return `Typed "${TYPED_IN_EDITOR}"; the tab shows unsaved changes.`;
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'S3',
			title: 'Another tool adds a cell to the file on disk',
			async run(context) {
				const onDisk = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(notebookPath, 'utf8'));
				onDisk.cells.push(cell('c3', 'code', ADDED_ON_DISK));
				fs.writeFileSync(notebookPath, JSON.stringify(onDisk, null, 1) + '\n');
				await context.page.waitForTimeout(2000);
				const rows = await context.page.locator(CELL_ROWS).count();
				return `The file on disk now has 3 cells; the dirty editor still shows ${rows}.`;
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'S4',
			title: 'Save: the conflict notification offers Compare',
			async run(context) {
				const { page } = context;
				await context.workbench.quickaccess.runCommand('workbench.action.files.save');
				const toast = await conflictToast(context);
				const buttons = await toastButtons(toast);
				if (!buttons.includes('Compare')) {
					throw new Error(`The save conflict notification offers only [${buttons.join(', ')}], no Compare.`);
				}
				for (const expected of ['Overwrite', 'Revert']) {
					if (!buttons.includes(expected)) {
						throw new Error(`The save conflict notification lost ${expected}: [${buttons.join(', ')}].`);
					}
				}
				return `The notification offers [${buttons.join(', ')}].`;
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'S5',
			title: 'Compare opens the notebook diff of the file on disk and the unsaved notebook',
			async run(context) {
				const { page } = context;
				const toast = await conflictToast(context);
				await toast.locator('.monaco-button', { hasText: 'Compare' }).first().click();
				const diff = page.locator('.notebook-text-diff-editor').first();
				await diff.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20000 });
				await page.waitForFunction(([added, typed]) => {
					const editor = document.querySelector('.notebook-text-diff-editor');
					const text = (editor?.textContent ?? '').replace(/\u00a0/g, ' ');
					return text.includes(added) && text.includes(typed);
				}, [ADDED_ON_DISK, TYPED_IN_EDITOR], { timeout: 20000 });
				const title = (await page.locator('.tabs-container .tab.active').first().innerText()).trim();
				return `The notebook diff editor "${title}" shows the cell added on disk and the unsaved edit.`;
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'S6',
			title: 'Overwrite and Revert stay available next to the diff',
			async run(context) {
				const { page } = context;
				const toast = await conflictToast(context);
				const buttons = await toastButtons(toast);
				if (!buttons.includes('Overwrite') || !buttons.includes('Revert')) {
					throw new Error(`After Compare the notification offers [${buttons.join(', ')}].`);
				}
				const onDisk = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(notebookPath, 'utf8'));
				if (onDisk.cells.length !== 3) {
					throw new Error(`Compare changed the file on disk: it has ${onDisk.cells.length} cells.`);
				}
				return `The file on disk is untouched; the notification still offers [${buttons.join(', ')}].`;
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'S7',
			title: 'Another change on disk while the diff is open shows up in it',
			async run(context) {
				const { page } = context;
				const onDisk = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(notebookPath, 'utf8'));
				onDisk.cells.push(cell('c4', 'code', CHANGED_AGAIN));
				fs.writeFileSync(notebookPath, JSON.stringify(onDisk, null, 1) + '\n');
				await page.waitForFunction(([again, typed]) => {
					const editor = document.querySelector('.notebook-text-diff-editor');
					const text = (editor?.textContent ?? '').replace(/\u00a0/g, ' ');
					return text.includes(again) && text.includes(typed);
				}, [CHANGED_AGAIN, TYPED_IN_EDITOR], { timeout: 20000 });
				return `The open diff now also shows "${CHANGED_AGAIN}" from disk next to the unsaved edit.`;
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'S8',
			title: 'Overwrite replaces the file on disk with the unsaved notebook',
			async run(context) {
				const { page } = context;
				const toast = await conflictToast(context);
				await toast.locator('.monaco-button', { hasText: 'Overwrite' }).first().click();
				await page.waitForFunction(() => !document.querySelector('.tabs-container .tab.dirty'), undefined, { timeout: 20000 });
				const sources = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(notebookPath, 'utf8')).cells.map(c => [].concat(c.source).join(''));
				const text = sources.join('\n');
				if (!text.includes(TYPED_IN_EDITOR) || text.includes(ADDED_ON_DISK) || text.includes(CHANGED_AGAIN)) {
					throw new Error(`After Overwrite the file on disk has: ${JSON.stringify(sources)}`);
				}
				return `The file on disk now has the unsaved notebook (${sources.length} cells) and nothing is left unsaved.`;
			}
		}
	]
};
```

</details>

## Validation

| Check | Command | Result |
|-------|---------|--------|
| Repro on `main` @ `c8a3f819b4a` | `node test/scenario/out/runScenario.js --dev repro.cjs` (3 runs) | ❌ fails 3/3 as expected at the Compare check: the save conflict notification offers only [Overwrite, Revert]. These runs were recorded before the last two steps were added; those steps only run after that check. |
| Repro with this PR | same (3 runs) | ✅ passes 3/3: the notification offers [Compare, Overwrite, Revert]; Compare opens the notebook diff showing the cell added on disk and the unsaved edit; Overwrite and Revert are still offered; a second cell added on disk while the diff is open shows up in it; after Overwrite the file on disk holds the unsaved notebook and nothing is left unsaved |
| Unit tests | `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/test/browser/storedFileWorkingCopy.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/test/common/fileOnDiskFileSystemProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/test/browser/storedFileWorkingCopyManager.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/test/browser/fileWorkingCopyManager.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/test/browser/untitledFileWorkingCopyManager.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/test/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.test.ts` | ✅ 124 passing. New tests: the save conflict offers Compare and reloads an open comparison before showing it; no Compare when the editor can't open a diff; the readonly provider reports changes of the file on disk while watched; the notebook diff recomputes when its original side changes while it's the active editor |
| Play-test: change on disk while the diff is in the background, Compare again, then Revert | `node test/scenario/out/runScenario.js --dev <play-test>.cjs` | ✅ the diff showed each change on disk; Revert left nothing unsaved and the notebook showed the file on disk |
| Play-test: `notebook.diff.enablePreview` off, or screen reader optimization toggled on, at runtime | same | ✅ Compare still offered and opened the notebook diff with the unsaved edit (the editor resolver still provides the notebook diff); Overwrite and Revert worked |
| Play-test: same, after the editor resolver re-reads its registrations | same | ✅ Compare not offered; Overwrite and Revert worked |
| Play-test: screen reader optimization on at startup | same | ✅ Compare opened the notebook diff with the unsaved edit |
| Play-test: text file save conflict | same | ✅ unchanged: [Compare, Overwrite]; Compare opened the text conflict editor with its accept and revert toolbar; accepting wrote the editor contents to disk |
| Type check | `npm run typecheck-client` | ✅ no errors |
| Lint | `npx eslint <changed files>` | ✅ no problems |
| Formatting | `node build/hygiene.ts <changed files>` | ✅ passed |

<sub>Found and fixed with automated exploratory testing. Draft until reviewed by a human.</sub>

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup registers the readonly file-on-disk filesystem provider
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new BlockStartup contribution constructs one provider and registers it with IFileService before startup can proceed; construction performs only emitter/object allocation and provider-map registration.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant: one provider registration per workbench window, independent of files, editors, or workspace size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single registration; no queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No content cache is created or warmed. Registration only makes the scheme available; file content and watchers remain lazy until a comparison opens.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed constructor and registration call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact contribution-framework overhead is not measured, but the changed constructor has no scaling work or expensive boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds constant, lightweight startup work and defers all file reads and watches until use.

Scenarios.Scenario: A stored notebook save detects FILE_MODIFIED_SINCE and offers Compare
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The failed save's existing filesystem write completes with a conflict first. The diff then synchronously checks provider availability, finds the current working-copy editor, and scans registered diff-capable editor descriptors before constructing the notification action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The pre-existing save/write that returns FILE_MODIFIED_SINCE
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized write attempt per explicit or automatic save
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same save write occurred and the error notification offered only Overwrite and Revert.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It must fail before the Compare action is offered, but this boundary existed before the PR.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One check per save-conflict notification; the scan scales with registered editor descriptors, a bounded application registry rather than notebook cells or workspace files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous registry lookup and array scan. The existing save attempt remains serialized by the working-copy save sequencer; the diff adds no filesystem/IPC call until the user invokes Compare.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider/editor registrations are already in memory. There is no cold-vs-warm boundary difference for merely offering the action.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from getCompareEditorId and EditorResolverService.getEditors implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of third-party editor registrations varies, but the conflict path is infrequent and the scan does not cross a process or I/O boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added work on the save-error path is bounded in-memory registry work.

Scenarios.Scenario: The user invokes Compare for a notebook save conflict
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Compare reloads any already-open readonly working copy, then waits for editorService.openEditor. A warm virtual working copy reload performs virtual stat/read operations that delegate to the original filesystem; a cold comparison resolves the original while opening the editor. Notebook deserialization and initial diff computation must complete to render useful content.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat and read the underlying on-disk resource through FileOnDiskFileSystemProvider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One delegated read sequence per cold resolve or warm forced reload for each exact-resource working-copy type
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no Compare action and therefore no readonly-resource stat/read path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected Compare action awaits warm reloads and then editor opening, so these operations are on its display critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the requested diff editor and, for notebook editors, resolve serializer/model services that may cross extension-host or worker boundaries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One openEditor request per Compare click; notebook serialization/diff work is one logical operation for the notebook, not per cell boundary calls
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The save-conflict notification did not open a comparison.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The editor must open and compute its initial model/diff before the comparison is usable.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is one virtual resource per compared notebook and normally one working copy for its notebook type; getAll can include one entry per distinct working-copy type for that exact URI. File bytes and notebook cells control read, deserialize, and diff cost.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing virtual working copies are reloaded sequentially by the changed loop. StoredFileWorkingCopyManager serializes resolves per resource. Different concurrently opened conflict comparisons can proceed independently, but user action normally creates one/few.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold: no virtual working copy exists, so openEditor creates and reads it once. Warm: the loop forces one ETag-aware reload so an existing comparison is current, and editor opening reuses that model. There is no retained byte cache in the provider; unchanged reloads can terminate through ETag validation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the compare loop, provider delegation, working-copy map keyed by exact URI/type, and per-resource resolve serialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Notebook files can be large and provider implementations can be remote, but this cost is explicitly user-requested, has exact-resource cardinality, and is not multiplied by workspace size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the I/O and diff work are necessary for the requested comparison and remain bounded to the selected resource; no realistic large fan-out is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: An open conflict comparison tracks subsequent on-disk notebook changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A provider watch forwards a real-resource change to the virtual URI. The clean virtual working copy is reloaded and deserialized; its merged notebook content event now invokes updateLayout even while the diff editor is active, causing one notebook worker diff and, when changed, view-model/list reconstruction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and maintain a correlated watcher for the underlying file (remote providers can route this through the filesystem channel)
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One underlying watch per distinct active virtual file; identical outer watches are reference-counted by FileService
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No file-on-disk virtual resource or watcher existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Watcher setup is part of model lifetime, while individual notifications initiate the update path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload and deserialize the changed readonly notebook resource
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one running and one queued reload per exact resource; ETag suppresses unchanged content
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The conflict comparison did not exist; for other notebook diffs, existing working-copy reload behavior supplied model changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new file contents must load before the diff can reflect the external change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute the notebook diff in the notebook editor worker
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker request per merged original-notebook content event; not per cell
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: While the diff editor was active, original-side changes were suppressed by the combined listener's active-editor guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The active diff cannot update until the worker result returns; UI reconstruction follows only when the diff changed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with changed-file event frequency, notebook byte size, and cell count. Notebook reset batches raw edits into one onDidChangeContent event. The working-copy reload queue is capped at one running plus one queued resolve per resource.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One correlated underlying watcher per actively watched virtual resource after FileService deduplication of identical outer watches. Reloads are serialized and coalesced to queue size two per resource. updateLayout cancels stale consumers; the worker request itself may finish, but one batched content event is emitted per completed reload.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The watcher is created only while the virtual resource is watched and disposed with that watch. Reloads send the prior ETag, so unchanged events avoid deserialization and diff events. There is no negative cache; missing/deleted state follows existing working-copy handling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from provider watch delegation, FileService watcher deduplication, working-copy queue bounds, NotebookTextModel pauseable event batching, and the changed original-side listener.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large notebooks or slow remote files make each update expensive, and exact external-write frequency is workload-dependent. However, reset events are batched, unchanged reads are ETag-checked, and per-resource reload accumulation is explicitly bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the newly performed diff is required to keep an active comparison current, and realistic event multiplicity is batched/coalesced rather than per-cell or unbounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. Traced startup registration, conflict-action eligibility, comparison open/reload, watcher lifecycle, delegated filesystem/IPC boundaries, notebook event batching, per-resource resolve coalescing, worker diff computation, and disposal. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not itself establish a concrete shipped performance-regression fix requiring blame.
